title: Runtime.start must persist custom_domain across redeploys (currently discards it -> domain wiped on cutover)
description: Deploy.Runtime.start builds registry attrs as %{release_snapshot, service_vm_id, url, port} with NO custom_domain, so registry_put on every deploy OVERWRITES the entry and wipes custom_domain. Result: even with the reconciler path set up, the FIRST redeploy drops the domain. This is the linchpin of redeploy-safety.
design: Thread custom_domain through Runtime.start (read the prior registry entry and preserve custom_domain, or accept it as an opt) so registry_put keeps it. Then Runtime.start's existing RouteReconciler.trigger() re-emits the route with the new vm_id's derived backend automatically. Verify with an actual redeploy: domain keeps serving, no gateway.toml touch.
acceptance_criteria: After 'mj domain set', a full redeploy (new service VM + IP) keeps the app serving at its fqdn with zero manual gateway edits; registry entry retains custom_domain across the cutover.
notes:
CONFIRMED FROM SOURCE (migration 2026-07-20): Runtime.start.finish/9 (runtime.ex:126) builds attrs WITHOUT :custom_domain -> Registry.put/build_entry constructs a fresh Entry with custom_domain=nil and write_atomic overwrites the JSON -> redeploy WIPES custom_domain. Then runtime.ex:134 RouteReconciler.trigger() re-renders, but desired_specs filters on is_binary(custom_domain), so the app no longer qualifies and its route is DROPPED -> app falls off the gateway after ANY redeploy. Backend re-derivation is fine (reconciler computes allocate_ip(vm_id):port from the CURRENT vm_id — verified). FIX (small): in finish/9 read the prior entry's custom_domain (ops.registry_get is already wired at runtime.ex:300) and carry it into attrs. Once fixed, redeploys auto-update the route with no gateway.toml touch. HARD PREREQUISITE for the whole domain epic. LIVE IMPACT: startupcentral.build is on the reconciler path now, so its NEXT redeploy will drop the domain until this ships.
LANDED IN CODE (main, commit 1c0f520): runtime.ex finish/ now carries custom_domain forward via preserved_custom_domain/2 (reads prior entry via ops.registry_get) + start/4 gained an explicit custom_domain: opt for first-time set. 3 tests. NOT yet deployed to server (needs orchestrator redeploy).

title: VM durability: make 'disappeared forever' structurally impossible
description: A user VM (1GB) OOM'd during a build; the recovery reboot hit a transient virtiofsd resource error and the VM's BTRFS subvolume + StateStore record were permanently deleted. Root cause: multiple code paths hard-delete the rootfs subvolume (the source of truth for a VM's data), and one path (Health.nuke/1) deletes BEFORE confirming a replacement can be built. This epic hardens every destruction path so a transient failure can never cause permanent data loss.

Follow-ups: mjolnir-s8h (blocking startup reconcile), mjolnir-5fu (stale ghost records). Classifier hardened for TAP-busy (commit 2a86b09, needs redeploy).

title: VM.spawn: plumb owner_id + extra_mounts (both silently ignored today) — unblocks owned build VMs + virtio-fs source ingest
description: Found during the first real deploy (startup-central, 2026-07-19): passing owner_id or extra_mounts to Mjolnir.VM.spawn via rpc is SILENTLY IGNORED (they're in @config_key_allowlist but not plumbed to the boot path). Consequences: (1) rpc-spawned build VMs have owner=nil, so the owner-scoped /api/vms/:id/exec 404s -> can't use 'mj exec' (the reliable vsock channel); had to fall back to serial-console VM.exec which is UNRELIABLE for multi-line/long build commands. (2) extra_mounts is ignored, so the virtio-fs source-share ingest doesn't work; had to copy source into the rootfs subvolume host-side as a hack.
design: Plumb owner_id and extra_mounts through VM.spawn -> child_spec -> boot config -> Cloud Hypervisor (extra virtiofsd via VirtioFS.start_many; guest mounts by tag). With owner_id honored, build VMs are owned -> mj exec (vsock, handles multi-line/long) works. With extra_mounts honored, the Builder can mount the app source read-only instead of copying into the rootfs. Add tests.
acceptance_criteria: VM.spawn(%{owner_id: X, extra_mounts: [%{tag,shared_dir}]}) produces a VM owned by X with the share mounted; mj exec works on it.

title: mj domain set/rm/ls + /api/domains — merge-aware custom_domain update + trigger reconcile
description: No CLI/API exists to manage app domains today (only hand-edited gateway.toml). Add 'mj domain set <app> <fqdn>', 'mj domain rm <app>', 'mj domain ls' backed by a new HTTP API, since there is currently no /api/deploy or /api/domains surface at all (router.ex has nothing).

Server: merge-aware Registry update (Registry.put appears to REPLACE the Entry from attrs, so read-modify-write to avoid wiping service_vm_id/url/port), set custom_domain+port, then RouteReconciler.trigger(). ls joins registry + live VMs to show app -> fqdn -> backend(guest_ip:port) -> cert status. The CLI must surface this as a hard error, not a silent no-op. (3) render_and_reload() is synchronous (returns the routes) vs trigger() debounced — the API should confirm the route landed in apps.toml before returning success.

title: mj domain — reconciler-driven custom-domain management for deployed apps
description:
Give deployed apps a first-class custom domain via the CLI, driven by the route reconciler so it survives redeploys. Today (proven manually with startupcentral.build, 2026-07-20): routes are set by hand-editing /etc/mjolnir/gateway.toml + SIGHUP; the mj CLI has NO route/domain/app-deploy commands and there is no HTTP API for it. The reconciler machinery (Gateway.Routes/RouteReconciler unions Deploy.Registry.custom_domain + :gateway_extra_domains -> apps.toml, re-derives backend from vm_id on every deploy/VM event) is fully built but nothing populates custom_domain and the apex must be pre-registered in :gateway_apexes.

## Context
Grounded in the startup-central first-customer deploy to mjolnir (2026-07-19/20). startupcentral.build is currently a hand-written gateway.toml [[route]] (pinned to the service VM's guest IP -> breaks on next redeploy); this epic replaces that pattern.
design: End state: 'mj domain set <app> <fqdn>' persists custom_domain on the registry (merge-aware), ensures the apex is registered (gateway_apexes + a [[domain]] + cert in gateway config), and triggers a reconcile. Backend re-derivation is already free from the reconciler. Three sub-problems: (1) persist custom_domain incl. across redeploys, (2) dynamic apex registration without an orchestrator restart, (3) per-domain cert provisioning (ACME if the Cloudflare token covers the zone, else install a provided Cloudflare Origin CA cert via [[cert]]).
acceptance_criteria: mj domain set <app> <fqdn> makes the app serve at <fqdn> with TLS; a subsequent redeploy (new service VM/IP) keeps serving at <fqdn> with NO manual gateway edits; mj domain ls shows app->fqdn->backend->cert; mj domain rm removes it.
notes: STATUS 2026-07-20: startupcentral.build MIGRATED to the reconciler path live (zero downtime) — proves the architecture. But it exposed two live fragilities that this epic must close: (A) redeploy wipes custom_domain [12.1, now P0] and (B) orchestrator restart drops the runtime-only apex [12.3]. Until both ship, startupcentral.build's route survives only as long as there's no app redeploy AND no orchestrator restart (apex held via runtime put_env; route reconciler-managed). config.exs:76 gateway_apexes still lists only the original 3 apexes.

Each fixture doubles as living documentation of what the platform supports. Extends gge.1.8's ExUnit :integration infra; server-gated.

title: DB migrations as a first-class deploy phase — auto-run, never SSH-in-manually
description:
Migrations are where 'automatic feel' lives or dies: if you have to SSH in and run db:migrate by hand, the deploy layer has failed. Add a migrate phase to the deploy pipeline: an optional manifest key (e.g. [deploy] migrate = "bun run db:migrate" in mjolnir.toml, or detected from drizzle/prisma/rails conventions later) that runs against the app's PERSISTENT database after files are in place and before the release goes live (before the symlink flip in release-dir mode / before cutover in fresh-VM mode). Failure aborts the release — the previous release keeps serving, and the error surfaces as an app failure, not a platform one.

Ordering subtleties to design: migrations run in the RUN environment (the stateful VM, where the real db lives), not the build VM — build layers must never touch state (also keeps them cacheable + secret-free per the initiative doc's hard rule). Pair with the pre-deploy btrfs snapshot from gge.7 so a bad migration is state-rollbackable, not just code-rollbackable. Zine's flow (drizzle: bun run db:generate committed, bun run db:migrate applied at deploy) is the reference case.

title: Design: stateful-app deploy model — Capistrano-style releases on a persistent VM
description:
The fresh-VM-per-deploy cutover (Deploy.Runtime P0) wipes on-VM state — a stateful app like Zine keeps its SQLite db (subscribers, send ledger) on the rootfs, so every deploy would destroy it. But statefulness is one of Mjolnir's differentiators: VMs persist, and btrfs snapshots make that persistence cheap and rollbackable. Design a second deploy mode that embraces it.

Proposed model (Capistrano-style, per Duke): the app VM is long-lived; a deploy places the new build into a timestamped release dir (/app/releases/<ts>) and atomically re-points a 'current' symlink; the unit's WorkingDirectory follows the symlink. Rollback = re-point the symlink to the previous release (instant, no rebuild). Transport-agnostic: tar upload, git pull, scp — anything that gets files into the release dir works. Durable state (sqlite db, uploads) lives OUTSIDE releases (e.g. /app/shared) and is linked in, Capistrano-style.

Decide: (1) how this composes with the layer-cache Builder — build in the ephemeral build VM as today, then sync the built artifact into the stateful VM's release dir (build stays cached/reproducible; run VM keeps identity+state)? (2) per-app mode selection: stateless apps keep fresh-VM cutover (immutable, blue/green-ish), stateful apps get release-dir mode — detector/manifest chooses. (3) btrfs snapshot of the app VM pre-deploy as the state-level rollback complement to the symlink flip. (4) health gating before the flip (relates gge.5).
notes: Design direction (discussed 2026-07-01): Capistrano's pointer-flip survives; its two failures (no env reproducibility, shared/-dir-by-convention) are both solved by Mjolnir primitives — layer-cache builder supplies reproducible envs; a NESTED btrfs subvolume for /data is structurally excluded from rootfs snapshots (snapshots aren't recursive), making the durable-state contract filesystem-enforced instead of conventional. Core tension: code rolls back, data rolls forward — keep the axes separately addressable; never auto-revert data. Recommended model: long-lived VM; releases/<ts> + current symlink flip + unit restart (fast path, no reboot); rootfs snapshot pre-flip (safety net, reboot to revert, /data rides through); /data subvolume snapshot pre-migration (restore is manual + operator-confirmed — it discards writes). Migrations run between placement and flip; failure aborts, old release keeps serving; expand/contract as documented contract. SQLite: wal_checkpoint before data snapshots for clean copies. Blue-green = the STATELESS mode (fresh-VM cutover via gateway flip already is it); for local-SQLite apps it's theater (one writer). Steal health-gating for the stateful flip. DEFAULT = stateful — misclassification is asymmetric: stateless-treated-as-stateful accumulates a stale /data; stateful-treated-as-stateless loses the db. Manifest opts into stateless.

title: Managed (host-escrowed) secrets mode — dormancy-capable LUKS secrets

Unlike :persistent (passphrase held by a remote Iroh peer, host-blind, refuses dormancy), :managed lets the host autonomously unlock secrets on wake-on-message — enabling scale-to-zero for VMs with secrets. title: snapshot of running VM wedges guest + drops it from mj list; revive can't recover
description:
mj snapshot create on a RUNNING VM reports success but (1) can leave the guest wedged (CH pause/resume; sshd/app/Iroh hang while CH vm.info=Running), (2) makes the VM vanish from mj list/info/url, and (3) mj revive reports success but no-ops. Caused ~11min prod outage; only host-root 'curl ... vm.reboot' recovered it.

ROOT CAUSE (code-grounded):
- do_snapshot/3 (lib/mjolnir/vm.ex:1883) does sync->pause->btrfs snapshot->resume but NEVER verifies the guest recovered after resume. Returns success whenever BTRFS.create_snapshot is ok.
- VM.list/0 (vm.ex:189) drops any VM whose GenServer.call(:get_state, 5000) times out (catch :exit -> nil; reject nil). The VM is NOT de-registered — its GenServer mailbox is blocked behind a synchronous vsock call into the wedged guest (likely a Health.Monitor heal). The 5002ms log line is this exact timeout.
- revive/1 (vm.ex:264) only flips StateStore intent=:running. Reconcile.run (reconcile.ex:77,106) skips VMs with a live registry entry. The wedged VM is still registered -> revive is a guaranteed no-op for this failure mode.
- No CH reboot wrapper exists: client.ex has pause/resume/shutdown/delete/info/resize but no reboot_vm; no reboot_instance behaviour callback; no mj reboot/restart command.

FIX PLAN:
1. do_snapshot health-verify: post-resume guest ping; on failure attempt vm.reboot+re-ping; report degraded/error loudly instead of 'created successfully'.
2. list/0 (and info/url): on :get_state timeout include the VM marked degraded/unreachable rather than omitting it.
3. Add reboot plumbing: Client.reboot_vm (PUT /api/v1/vm.reboot) -> reboot_instance callback -> VM.reboot/1 -> POST /api/vms/:id/reboot -> mj reboot/restart.
4. revive/1: detect alive-but-wedged (live GenServer + unreachable guest agent) and reboot+re-attach instead of no-op.
5. Fix ~5s GET /api/vms stall: stop guest-blocking heals from running inside the VM GenServer mailbox / bound+parallelize liveness probes so :get_state is never starved.
notes:
VERIFIED END-TO-END on deployed server (2026-06-26, restart 03:15:58 UTC, incl. 19af2a8):
- spawn -> exec ok
- snapshot create -> success; post-snapshot exec ok (vsock conn rebuild)
- mj reboot -> 'guest healthy, control plane re-attached'; exec after reboot ok with uptime 'up 0 min' (proves clean restart from preserved rootfs, NOT destroyed); VM stays running
- mj revive on healthy live VM -> ok no-op, VM still responsive
- list shows VMs correctly throughout; prod VM 076adf62 untouched
All core fixes confirmed working in production. Reboot race fixed by the terminate-cleanup hardening. Closing.
close_reason: Closed

title: Builder executor — boot resume_from, exec+snapshot each layer, teardown (injectable-ops, macOS-unit-tested)
description: The VM/BTRFS execution half of Deploy.Builder, sibling to the pure planner (gge.1.4.1). Mjolnir.Deploy.Builder.build/3 takes base_layer_id + ordered steps (each with precomputed input_hash), derives existing layers from BTRFS snapshots, calls Plan.compute, then: full cache hit -> no VM; else boot one ephemeral VM from resume_from (base image when resume==base, else deploy-<key> snapshot), exec each steps_to_run command via VM.exec and snapshot the result to its content-addressed key, always tear the VM down. Drives VM/BTRFS through an injectable ops seam so the boot->exec->snapshot->teardown choreography is unit-tested on macOS with fakes; real captures (VM.spawn/exec/snapshot/stop, BTRFS.list_snapshots) are server-gated. exec surfaces non-zero exits as {:error,{:exit_code,..}}, so failed build steps abort + teardown.

Effects behind injectable ops map (default = VM.spawn/exec/snapshot/stop + BTRFS.list_snapshots); fakes record call order in tests. Layer id <-> 'deploy-'<>key translation owned here; planner stays name-agnostic. exec non-zero exit -> {:error,{:exit_code,..}} aborts build. title: Forgejo runner leaks VMs: teardown StopVM uses cancelled job context, DELETE fails on cancel/timeout/shutdown
description: ROOT CAUSE of the leaked CI VMs (see cdz). native/forgejo-runner/pkg/mjolnir/executor.go VMEnvironment.Remove() issued the StopVM DELETE /api/vms/:id on the inherited job context. act runs Remove/Close via Finally(), so on a cancelled job, a timed-out job, or a runner restart (shutdown force-cancels in-progress jobs with shutdown_timeout=0s — confirmed in journalctl), the ctx is already cancelled and net/http fails the DELETE immediately with 'context canceled'. The VM is never destroyed; Mjolnir durability (r84) then resurrects the orphaned :running record on every restart, so owner=localhost CI VMs accumulate (found 16 live leaked on root@45.76.77.97, 2026-06-24). Normal completions clean up fine (live ctx), so it is a slow leak.
design: Detach teardown from the job context: context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 60s) for the StopVM DELETE so cleanup always reaches the API even when the inherited ctx is dead. Mjolnir client carries its own base-URL/auth (localhost bypass), so dropping inherited ctx values is safe. Fixes both Remove() and Close() (Close calls Remove).
acceptance_criteria: A cancelled or timed-out CI job still results in its VM being destroyed (mj list / localhost /api/vms returns to baseline); runner restart during a job does not leak the job's VM.
notes: DEPLOYED + LIVE 2026-06-25: fix merged to main (725f802) and shipped via full deploy (deploy + deploy-gateway + deploy-runner). forgejo-runner restarted on the new binary (declared successfully), gateway + mjolnir core verified healthy, VM 076adf62 survived the restart, total VM count back to 1 (restart leaked nothing). REMAINING (left open): end-to-end proof — run a CI job and cancel it (or restart the runner mid-job) and confirm the job's VM is destroyed rather than leaked. The fix is active; this is observational confirmation only.

title: Builder cache-decision planner (pure, macOS-verifiable) — step chain + existing layers → resume point + steps to run
description: The pure core of Deploy.Builder, extractable and unit-testable with no VM. Given a base layer id, an ordered list of build steps (each with a precomputed input_hash), and the set of already-existing layer ids, compute: the chained cache_key per layer (via Mjolnir.Deploy.CacheKey.compute, chaining parent→child), which layers are cache HITS vs MISSES, the deepest contiguous cached prefix (resume_from), the steps that still need to run, and the final release_layer_id. Key property to lock in tests: because keys chain on the parent layer id, the hit set is ALWAYS a contiguous prefix — a downstream key can never spuriously hit once an ancestor changed. The VM/BTRFS execution half of gge.1.4 (boot resume_from, run steps via VM.exec, snapshot each) stays open and server-gated.
notes: Pure function over data; caller precomputes input_hash with CacheKey.hash_file/hash_tree (keeps FS access out of the planner). Defines the data shape the server-side executor will consume.
close_reason: Mjolnir.Deploy.Builder.Plan implemented: pure cache-decision planner (chained keys, structural contiguous-prefix hit invariant, resume_from/steps_to_run/release_layer_id). 9 tests incl. the downstream-key-must-not-hit case. VM/BTRFS execution half of gge.1.4 stays open + server-gated.

title: Deploy.Builder — run ordered build plan in ephemeral VM, snapshot + cache each layer
description: The frame of the deploy layer. Given a build plan: boot an ephemeral VM from the base (or parent layer on cache hit = reflink clone + skip), run each step via Mjolnir.VM.exec, snapshot the result via VM.snapshot/Mjolnir.BTRFS, content-address it with the cache-key module. title: mj deploy — Heroku-style 'git push and it's live' app deploy layer (snapshot-layer PaaS)
description: Implement the 'mj deploy' layer specified in docs/plans/initiatives/mjolnir-deploy.md. In an app dir, 'mj deploy' should — zero-config for the common case — build the app inside a microVM, snapshot every build step (BTRFS reflink layer cache) so rebuilds are instant, boot the result as a supervised service, and return a live HTTPS URL. Builds on Forge (run-state reconciliation, NOT the chassis), Sites, gateway, mise, and the VM snapshot/dormancy machinery. The frame is a NEW snapshot-layer builder; Forge is a component. Child tasks track the doc's phasing P0–P3 plus the parallel recrypt track.
design: Two-phase model (load-bearing): BUILD is imperative/ordered/non-idempotent → snapshot-layer builder (each step → content-addressed BTRFS snapshot, cache key = hash(parent_layer + step_cmd + input_hash)); RUN-STATE is declarative/convergent → Forge resources (systemd_unit/file/user) reconciled inside the guest over vsock exec. New modules: Mjolnir.Deploy.Supervisor {Detector, Builder, Runtime, Registry}, POST /api/deploy, 'mj deploy' client subcommand (distinct from existing 'mj server deploy' which runs scripts/deploy.sh).
notes: No code exists yet as of 2026-06-24. Design doc at docs/plans/initiatives/mjolnir-deploy.md (commits 6ecab5f, 9d74b8e, 56ec216). Decided: tar-the-cwd source ingest (front door) + first-class private-repo deploy-key pull; qgroup-metered layer GC with two GC classes; secrets re-inject on wake + render-to-tmpfs now, recrypt-to-VM-key as end-state. Resist scope gravity into a general PaaS — the zero-config moment is the product, not feature count.

title: StartupReconcile blocks API availability proportional to VM count
description: During server verification of mjolnir-r84: with 18 stranded :running records, the blocking StartupReconcile child resumes all VMs synchronously (~3s each) BEFORE Bandit/the HTTP API starts, so the public API was unreachable for ~60s after restart (connection refused). Make reconcile non-blocking (or parallelize resumes, or start the API before reconcile) so API availability is independent of stranded-VM count. Found while verifying the durability epic on root@45.76.77.97.
design: Two levers, both applied: (1) StartupReconcile child changed from blocking Mjolnir.Startup.run to a concurrent {Task,:start_link,...} so the supervisor reaches Bandit immediately — ordering still holds since Cleanup sweep + registries are earlier siblings; (2) Reconcile.run/0 resumes via Task.async_stream with :reconcile_max_concurrency (default 4, timeout :infinity) instead of serial Enum.each; (3) execute/1 wraps resume in try/catch so an await_boot exit can't abort the async_stream batch. Stranded VMs already show state=recovering in /api/vms; Health.Monitor 30s tick is the safety net.
close_reason: Implemented in 845a1a3 (branch fix/s8h-reconcile-nonblocking): reconcile off the blocking boot path + bounded-parallel resumes. 613 unit tests pass. Full server-restart-with-stranded-VMs verification rides the pending r84 KVM integration run.

title: Storage seam: Sites.Store → recrypt-storage (NIF vs sidecar spike + impl)
description:
Replace the STUBBED local Elixir chunk store (Mjolnir.Sites.Store, lib/mjolnir/sites/store.ex — verify_bao! is stubbed) with calls into recrypt-storage, which already implements content-addressed put/get WITH Bao outboards (put_with_outboard/get_with_outboard) and is e2e-tested against Minio.

## Why
The hardest stub (Bao outboard content-addressing) is already done and tested in Rust. Reimplementing it in Elixir is wasted effort and a second crypto implementation to keep correct.

## Spike first (the real decision)
Prove Sites.Store can round-trip ONE chunk (put_with_outboard then get_with_outboard, verifying hash) through recrypt-storage. Decide integration shape:
- NIF (rustler) — in-process, fastest, but couples BEAM to OpenFHE/aws-sdk build.
- Sidecar (recrypt-server HTTP, already exists) — looser coupling, network hop, separate process to supervise.
Recommend trying sidecar first (recrypt-server already runs an HTTP API) unless latency demands a NIF.

## Acceptance
- Sites.Store.put/get delegate to recrypt-storage (no stubbed verify).
- Bao verification is real (bytes failing hash never land).
- Round-trip test passes against a local backend.
- Decision (NIF vs sidecar) recorded in the issue + design doc.
notes: DEPLOYABILITY: prod compile exit 0; full mix test 600/0; Sites.Supervisor boots safe (default backend = Sites.Storage.Local, recrypt backend only if MJOLNIR_RECRYPT_STORAGE_URL set). SERVER RUNBOOK to go live: (1) in recrypt repo, add 4 content-addressed chunk routes to recrypt-server that round-trip a PRECOMPUTED outboard: PUT/GET /storage/blob/b3/{hash} and {hash}.obao (1:1 with put/get_with_outboard); current POST /files is multisig-gated, hashes server-side, stores empty outboard. (2) build+run recrypt-server on 45.76.77.97. (3) export MJOLNIR_RECRYPT_STORAGE_URL=http://127.0.0.1:7222. (4) validate: mix test test/mjolnir/sites/storage/recrypt_test.exs --include recrypt_storage.

title: Complete IdentiKey Sites: real publish path (storage→crypto→keyspace→transport→CLI)
description:
Make IdentiKey Sites actually work end-to-end so a user can: get an Iroh address, sign content with their IdentiKey, and publish static assets publicly / to recipients / to a keyspace — with everything durably backed by Backblaze B2.

## Why
Sites is a carefully-shaped scaffold with stubbed security-critical guts (Bao verify, manifest/HEAD signing, decrypt, Iroh bind all STUBBED). The design (docs/plans/initiatives/identikey-sites.md) is sound and the hard crypto already exists in ~/work/IdentiKey/recrypt. The work is integration, not invention.

## Layering (confirmed against both repos)
- Storage / 'Vault' = recrypt-storage crate (local.rs/s3.rs, aws_sdk_s3, outboard-aware, e2e-tested vs Minio). B2 = same code, B2 endpoint.
- Keyspace / recipients = identikey-storage-auth crate (keyspace.rs, capability.rs, grant.rs) + recrypt-core PRE (post-quantum).
- Serving / naming / provenance = Mjolnir.Sites (Iroh endpoint, HEAD pointer, OpenTimestamps, gateway).

## Product principle (drives the CLI child)
Common case must require ZERO special vocabulary: 'mjolnir publish ./dist' is public-by-default and returns a URL. Verifiability is a property you GET, not a feature you invoke. Recipients/keyspace are progressive-disclosure flags. No Norse codenames in the user surface; module stays Mjolnir.Sites internally.

## B2 invariant
Every published chunk + manifest must eventually land in Backblaze B2 (durable offsite). Local FS/BTRFS is the hot tier; B2 is the durable backing via recrypt-storage's S3 backend (endpoint_url + force_path_style, same as its minio() ctor).

## Out of critical path
OpenTimestamps (anchoring) and BTRFS-send replication stay deferred — not required for publish+serve.

## Related (do not duplicate)
mjolnir-89y (PG backfill), mjolnir-fn4 (HeadIndex hot serve), mjolnir-3ku (vault package mirror).
notes: LIVE STATUS (2026-06-23): Public-mode publish fully working in prod. Deploy clean (iroh 1.0 guest-agent rebuild OK, NRestarts=0, Bandit bound after 17-VM reconcile ~68s). E2E verified: signing (.3), Local storage (.1), serve/decrypt, and auto-register (.7) all green live. DONE: .2 (B2 scripts, install pending), .3, .6, .7. REMAINING (server-side): .1 go-live (4 recrypt-server chunk routes for recrypt/B2 backend — Local backend works today), .4 host Iroh bind (note: iroh now 1.0), .5 keyspace/recipient modes. Orphaned tiny test sites left in @sites under random fps (e2e/e2e2) — GC later.

title: Fix syslog vsock transport: route through guest agent channel 2
description: The guest-side syslog-vsock-forwarder.sh uses socat VSOCK-CONNECT:2:5001 (direct vsock connection to host port 5001), but the host-side Syslog.Listener receives data on vsock protocol channel 2 (the multiplexed binary channel within Mjolnir.Vsock.Connection). There is no raw vsock listener on port 5001 — the guest forwarder will get connection refused. Fix: add a syslog forwarding mode to the Rust guest agent (native/mjolnir_guest_agent) that reads from /dev/log and sends lines over vsock channel 2 using the existing wire protocol. Update scripts/ci-image/syslog-vsock.service to start the guest agent in syslog-forwarder mode instead of socat. Remove the socat-based forwarder script.
close_reason: Guest agent now binds /dev/log and forwards syslog on vsock channel 2. Socat forwarder removed.

title: forge: Declarations loader + DSL macros
description: Mjolnir.Forge.Declaration DSL (use macro) accumulating resources via module attributes. Mjolnir.Forge.Declarations module loads forge/declarations/*.exs at boot, watches via :file_system, re-evaluates on edit, registers per-host resource lists. Supports systemd_unit/2 macro for v0 (other kinds added with their tickets).
design: Open question per doc: forge/declarations/ vs config/. Going with forge/declarations/<host>.exs for now — keeps unit-file content diffable as separate files referenced via File.read! from declarations. Decision flagged separately.
acceptance_criteria: A forge/declarations/<host>.exs with two systemd_unit blocks evaluates to a list of 2 declared resources retrievable via Mjolnir.Forge.Declarations.for_host("<host>"). Editing the file triggers a reload event on the EventBus.
notes: ~150 LOC. Depends on resource behaviour being defined (for the macro to register kind modules).

File-watching is a v1 ticket.

title: forge: Diff engine (three-way compute)
description: Mjolnir.Forge.Diff.compute/3 takes (declared, owned, observed) maps keyed by {kind, id} and returns a list of {kind, id, status, declared_hash, owned_hash, observed_hash} per the design's 8-row matrix. Statuses: converged, drifted, missing, new, prune, conflict, unmanaged, plus the (cleared-ownership) tombstone row.
design: Pure function — no I/O, no DB. Takes hashes (or content + hash). Caller upserts results into Repo. This is the load-bearing piece of the design; keep it side-effect-free so it's trivially testable.
acceptance_criteria: Property test: every (declared,owned,observed) cell of {present,absent} × {present,absent} × {present,differs,absent} maps to the documented status. Unit test: a 3-resource declared set + a 1-resource owned set + a 5-resource observed set produces correct row classifications.
close_reason: Landed: Mjolnir.Forge.Diff.compute/3 — pure function over the 8-row matrix. Auto-adopt-on-exact-match implemented (decision per mjolnir-f7e). 11 unit tests cover every matrix cell + content propagation + multi-key fanout. 0 failures.

title: forge: Resource behaviour + SystemdUnit impl
description: Define Mjolnir.Forge.Resource behaviour (kind/0, id/1, canonical/1, observe_path/1, probe/2, apply/2, delete/2). Implement Mjolnir.Forge.Resource.SystemdUnit using {:file, /etc/systemd/system/<id>} observe, with apply = cp + systemctl daemon-reload + enable, delete = systemctl disable + rm. Canonical encoding uses :cbor with deterministic key ordering (RFC 8949 §4.2.1).
design: File-backed observe is preferred (cheap, uniform). Behaviour shape produces {:present, content} | :missing | {:error, _} from observe_one/3 regardless of path — diff engine doesn't branch on file vs probe.
acceptance_criteria: SystemdUnit can observe an existing unit file, produce a stable canonical CBOR encoding (same input → same bytes → same blake3 hash across runs), apply a new unit, and delete it. Behaviour callbacks documented.
notes: ~180 LOC for behaviour + SystemdUnit. New kinds in later tickets reuse this shape.
close_reason: Landed: Mjolnir.Forge.Resource behaviour with observe/3 dispatcher (file-backed vs probe) + Mjolnir.Forge.Resource.SystemdUnit (writes /etc/systemd/system/<id>, daemon-reload + enable + restart on apply, disable+rm on delete; v0 file-backed only). Canonical encoding via Mjolnir.Forge.Canonical (sorted-key JSON + SHA-256, no new deps).

title: forge: Supervisor + Repo + Ecto migrations
description: Mjolnir.Forge.Supervisor (one_for_one) under Mjolnir.Supervisor with: Mjolnir.Forge.Repo (Ecto + ecto_sqlite3, pool_size: 1, WAL mode), migrations for resources/events/host_meta schemas, SQLite at /var/lib/mjolnir/forge/state.db. Indexes on (host), (host,status), unique (host,kind,resource_id).
design: SQLite single-writer — serialize via pool_size:1 Repo. Mirrors Mjolnir.StateStore pattern. status enum: converged|drifted|missing|new|prune|unmanaged|conflict|ignored. action enum: create|update|delete|adopt|ignore|probe|error.
acceptance_criteria: App boots with Forge supervision tree. Repo migrates cleanly. Inserting/selecting a resources row via Repo works in iex. Survives BEAM restart (WAL recovery).
notes: Implementation note: design doc said ecto_sqlite3 but existing Mjolnir.StateStore is JSON-per-record + ETS. Following codebase convention — Forge.Store mirrors StateStore pattern at /var/lib/mjolnir/forge/state/<host>/<kind>_<id>.json. Canonical encoding: Jason with sorted keys. Hash: :crypto.hash(:sha256, ...) — no :cbor or :b3 dep needed.
close_reason: Landed: Mjolnir.Forge.Supervisor + Forge.Store (JSON+ETS, mirrors Mjolnir.StateStore) + Forge.Store.Record. Wired into Mjolnir.Application supervision tree. Config keys :forge_state_dir and :forge_declarations_path added. Compiles clean.

title: Forge: host config reconciler (umbrella)
description: Mjolnir.Forge is a declarative host config reconciler with three-way diff (declared/owned/observed), ownership tracking for prune, file+probe observe strategies, CBOR-over-HTTP API, Rust CLI, and (later) ratatui TUI. Design in docs/plans/host-reconcile.md (2026-05-12). v0 fixes the four drift items found in the 2026-05-11 host audit.
design: Three-way diff matrix is the entire state machine. Hash everything (blake3+canonical CBOR), materialize content only for diff display. Reconciler is server-side BEAM; Rust CLI is thin HTTP client over SSH-tunneled localhost — same pattern as 'mjolnir vm-spawn'. Apply is idempotent destroy-then-create. Ownership distinguishes prune from leave-alone — without it, removal is impossible.
acceptance_criteria: v0: 'mjolnir forge plan/apply/adopt --fzf' works against self host for systemd_unit kind. v1: full kind set + TUI + SSE + second (SSH) host. v2: on-host agent, HA controllers, web UI.
notes: Sizing per design doc: v0 ~1600 LOC (Elixir + Rust), TUI adds ~600 LOC, 2-3 focused days for v0.

title: Deploy build base image: node+bun+mise preinstalled (ci-style) so builds skip the ~30s toolchain install
description: The first deploy installed nodejs (apt) + bun (curl|bash) inside the build VM every time (~30s+, and the bun installer fails 'HOME: unbound variable' unless HOME=/root is exported). A prebaked base image (like ci-ubuntu-24.04 + bun) makes builds start from a warm toolchain, matching Detector's node@20/bun assumption.
design: Extend the CI image build (scripts/build-ci-image.sh pattern) to produce a 'deploy-node-bun' base with mise + node@20 + bun on PATH and HOME sane. Deploy.Builder spawns from it; install/build layers then key on lockfile/source hash over the warm base.
acceptance_criteria: A SvelteKit/adapter-node build on the deploy base needs no apt/bun install step; first-layer boot has node+bun ready.
notes: DONE (script) — scripts/build-deploy-base.sh added + merged to main (commit e4ae76e). Builds a 'deploy-node-bun' BTRFS base (mise + node@20 + bun, HOME=/root, shims symlinked to /usr/local/bin so bare 'sh -c' vsock exec resolves them). shellcheck-clean; NOT yet run on the server (needs root+Linux debootstrap) and NOT yet wired in. WAVE-2 WIRING (lib/, do in the /api/deploy or a Builder task): Deploy.Builder.build/3 takes :base_image (defaults to base_layer_id -> falls through to VM.spawn default 'ubuntu-24.04'); the deploy-lane caller (Deploy.Supervisor) must pass base_image/base_layer_id 'deploy-node-bun' or the new image is never used. Detector already emits 'mise install' as step 1 -> becomes a fast no-op on this base if the app pins node@20.

title: Per-domain cert provisioning: ACME-if-token-scoped, else install a provided Cloudflare Origin CA cert
description: TLS for a custom apex needs a cert the gateway serves. Gateway ACME (Let's Encrypt DNS-01) is PINNED to worldtree zones (the CF token's scope) — it can't auto-issue for arbitrary domains (e.g. identikey.io and startupcentral.build are both served via hand-installed [[cert]] blocks). So domain onboarding must support the manual/BYO-cert path as a first-class flow.
design: mj domain cert <fqdn> [--origin-ca <cert> <key> | --acme]. If the ACME token covers the zone, add fqdn to [acme].domains and let it issue. Else install a BYO cert (Cloudflare Origin CA, 15yr) to /etc/mjolnir/certs/<app>/ (owned by the gateway user 999:988, key 0600) + a [[cert]] block, SIGHUP reload. For Cloudflare-proxied apps this pairs with orange + Full(strict). startupcentral.build used exactly this (Origin CA) — codify it.
acceptance_criteria: mj domain cert installs/renews a serving cert for the fqdn; gateway presents it on SNI; Full(strict) via Cloudflare validates.

title: Dynamic apex registration (add fqdn apex to :gateway_apexes + [[domain]]) without an orchestrator restart
description: For the reconciler to emit a route for a new apex, the fqdn's apex must be in :gateway_apexes (orchestrator app-env) AND have a [[domain]] (+ serving cert) in the gateway. Both are static config today; adding an apex is a config-file edit. This is the hardest piece of domain automation.
design: Investigate: Application.put_env(:mjolnir, :gateway_apexes, ...) at runtime takes effect for the next reconcile without restart (reconciler reads configured_apexes() live) — but is lost on restart, so also persist to config durably. The gateway's [[domain]] block + fallthrough=none must be added to gateway.toml (or a reconciler-managed drop-in) and SIGHUP-reloaded. Decide whether apexes become reconciler-owned (generated) vs a managed list. NOTE: the migration task (startupcentral.build -> reconciler) will produce the definitive answer on restart-need + persistence; fold its findings in.
acceptance_criteria: Registering a new apex for a deployed app requires no orchestrator restart and survives one; reconciler emits the route and gateway serves it.
notes: MIGRATION FINDINGS (2026-07-20): Application.put_env(:mjolnir, :gateway_apexes, ...) DOES take effect live with no restart (reconciler reads configured_apexes/0 each render — verified). BUT it's EPHEMERAL: gateway_apexes is set at COMPILE TIME in config/config.exs:76 and baked into the released sys.config; there is NO env-var/runtime override. So on the next mjolnir.service restart the apex reverts and startupcentral.build's route is dropped -> downtime. Two-sided requirement per apex: Elixir :gateway_apexes (so split_fqdn matches) AND a Rust-side [[domain]] block in gateway.toml (drop-ins can't declare apexes; applies on SIGHUP, no restart). CORE FIX (biggest friction point): make :gateway_apexes RUNTIME-configurable (env var or a managed file read in runtime.exs) so adding a domain never needs an orchestrator recompile/redeploy. Durable-today fallback: edit config.exs:76 + rebuild/redeploy the release. CLI must own both the apex-list edit and the gateway.toml [[domain]] edit, and warn that persistence needs a redeploy until apexes are runtime-configurable.

title: Cut Zine over to mj deploy + managed secrets — retire manual git deploy and tmpfs inject
description:
The capstone migration: move Zine prod (currently VM 076adf62, manual git-reset/build/restart deploy, tmpfs secrets via scripts/mjolnir-inject-secrets.sh re-run after every reboot) onto the mj deploy flow with secrets_mode: :managed. Zine is the reference stateful app: bun + SvelteKit adapter-node + better-sqlite3 (trustedDependencies committed), drizzle migrations, local.db holds subscribers + newsletter send ledger (MUST survive deploys — needs gge.7 release-dir mode), non-secret /opt/app/.env config, AWS SES + Beehiiv creds (managed secrets, seeded once at /var/lib/mjolnir/zine-secrets.json per docs/runbooks/zine-managed-secrets-migration.md).

Cutover steps: (1) registry entry takes over zine.identikey.io (custom_domain+port landed 2026-07-01; remove the hardcoded gateway_extra_domains route in config/prod.exs:17 — l79.5); (2) seed host secrets file; (3) first mj deploy, verify (send a dry-run newsletter + test-list send before trusting it); (4) copy local.db into the new home with the old app quiesced (clean sqlite copy); (5) kill old VM, retire inject script, update Zine-repo bd memories (mjolnir-deploy-state, ticket refs). secrets_mode is fixed at spawn — no in-place conversion, hence new VM. NOT to be run near a newsletter send.

title: Deploy-path managed-secrets plumbing — per-app secrets file → spawn_opts on every deploy
description: Deploy.Runtime.start already passes spawn_opts through (secrets_mode: :managed + secrets payload work today — the zine-managed-secrets-migration runbook drives it by hand via rpc). What's missing is the orchestrator wiring: the deploy pipeline (gge.1.6) reads a per-app secrets file on the host (/var/lib/mjolnir/<app>-secrets.json, 0600, off the data volume) and folds {secrets_mode: :managed, secrets: creds} into the Runtime.start spawn_opts automatically. Because release snapshots carry no LUKS volume, secrets are re-supplied on every deploy from that host file — it is the source of truth; rotation = edit file + redeploy. Apply to RUNTIME spawn only, never Deploy.Builder (a LUKS volume in a build layer would be keyed to the throwaway build VM and baked into the snapshot). In release-dir mode (gge.7) the long-lived VM is spawned managed once, and deploys just re-render env if changed. Relates: gge.3 (tmpfs render — shipped), gge.6 (recrypt end-state replaces the host-held file).

title: deploy.sh --gateway is not gateway-only: always rebuilds + restarts Elixir
description:
scripts/deploy.sh gates the gateway BUILD behind --gateway (lines 208-214), but the Elixir release build (line 241 'mix release') and 'systemctl restart mjolnir' (line 254) are UNCONDITIONAL — they run on every invocation, including 'just deploy-gateway'. So there is no gateway-only mode: deploying the gateway also rebuilds and restarts the main Elixir process, which triggers the Cleanup-kills-VMs -> Reconcile-resumes-from-StateStore cycle (a brief downtime window for every running VM) and ships whatever Elixir code is on the tree.

EXPECTED: '--gateway' (and a 'just deploy-gateway') should build + install + restart ONLY mjolnir-gateway, leaving the Elixir service untouched. Symmetrically, a plain deploy should be able to skip the gateway. This matters for safe, isolated rollouts (validate a gateway change without bouncing all VMs).

FIX SKETCH: gate the Elixir build+restart (lines 238-254) behind a flag (e.g. default-on, but skipped when a new --gateway-only / --no-elixir flag is passed, OR make --gateway imply gateway-only unless combined with a full-deploy flag). Preserve current 'just deploy' (full) behavior; add 'just deploy-gateway' = gateway-only. Update the Justfile recipes + CLAUDE.md docs accordingly.

Found during gateway local-routing rollout (epic mjolnir-l79).

title: Fold gateway route generator into Forge (with gge.4 dynamic declarations)
description:
Replace the bespoke Mjolnir.Gateway.Routes write-file+systemctl-reload with a Forge-managed resource, so gateway routing converges/drifts/prunes like every other host resource instead of being a parallel reconciler. See docs/forge-architecture.md (Relationship to Deploy) + docs/plans/gateway-local-routing.md.

Effort assessment (from code review):
- FREE: the drop-in file IS a Forge 'file' resource — apply writes content+mode, drift diffs source bytes, delete prunes.
- EASY: reload-on-change — Forge only calls apply/3 on :new/:drifted/:missing (never :converged), so putting 'systemctl reload' inside a dedicated gateway_routes resource kind's apply (per resource.ex:15 'daemon-reload, ufw reload' pattern) fires ONLY when routes changed. No notify/handler machinery needed.
- THE REAL GAP: dynamic declarations. Forge declarations are static .exs files loaded from disk (Declarations compiles forge/declarations/*.exs; reload/0 re-reads disk). No runtime API to update a declaration when a VM starts/stops. Gateway routes are dynamic.

STRATEGIC: that dynamic-declaration capability is exactly what gge.4 (Forge-over-vsock deploy) needs — Deploy generates per-app run-state resources at deploy time. So build 'programmatic/in-memory declaration source' (e.g. Declarations.put_dynamic(host, resources) merged with file-based) for gge.4, and the gateway route generator becomes its first trivial consumer. Do NOT build it standalone. Blocked-on/with: deploy epic gge.4.

title: Deploy: --domain plumbing + backfill zine into Deploy.Registry
description:
Gateway local-routing epic (mjolnir-l79) is live. Two follow-ups to fully close the loop:
1. mj deploy --domain <fqdn>: plumb a custom domain through Deploy.Runtime so Deploy-managed apps set Registry.Entry.custom_domain (+port already recorded). Until then, Mjolnir.Gateway.Routes only auto-routes apps listed in :gateway_extra_domains.
2. Backfill zine into Deploy.Registry (custom_domain=zine.identikey.io, port=3000) OR migrate zine through Deploy.Runtime, then drop the pinned entry from config/prod.exs :gateway_extra_domains (its vm_id 076adf62 is hardcoded and will go stale if zine is re-provisioned).
Also: consider fixing the deploy.sh gateway preflight (Python tomllib check over ssh with nested quotes gives false-positive 'failed to parse' warnings — it doesn't reflect the Rust parser).

title: Gateway: Elixir route generator renders gateway.d/apps.toml from live VM state
description:
Phase 2 of gateway local-routing (docs/plans/gateway-local-routing.md). Depends on Phase 1 drop-in loader. Automatically keep local [[route]] entries fresh so co-located app VMs are served over local TCP (no Iroh), eliminating the ~7s cold-start (proven in Phase 0).

Design: new Mjolnir.Gateway.Routes module renders /etc/mjolnir/gateway.d/apps.toml: for each app with a custom domain whose VM is on THIS host, emit [[route]] apex/subdomain/backend where backend = <guest_ip>:<port>. Atomic write + reload (systemctl reload mjolnir-gateway once ExecReload is added, else systemctl kill -s HUP). Full re-render each time (small N), idempotent. Trigger on: deploy cutover (Deploy.Runtime after registry_put) + EventBus :vm_restored/:vm_started + Mjolnir boot.

CRITICAL findings from live validation:
- guest_ip is already exposed by GET /api/vms (and VM status) — READ IT, do not recompute Network.allocate_ip. Simpler and authoritative.
- zine is NOT in Deploy.Registry (manually provisioned). The generator must NOT assume every served app has a registry entry. Source of truth for domain→VM intent is currently only the gateway [[alias]]. Options: (a) backfill Deploy.Registry with a domain+VM for manual apps, (b) generate routes by joining existing [[alias]] entries (domain→ticket) to live VMs (ticket→guest_ip via /api/vms). Recommend: add custom_domain + port (structured) to Deploy.Registry.Entry AND make manual provisioning write a registry entry, so the registry is the single source of truth.
- guest_ip stable across restart/restore (vm_id preserved) but CHANGES on redeploy — regeneration on cutover is the point.
Acceptance: redeploy an app, gateway.d/apps.toml updates with new guest_ip, requests log route=local; restart host → routes regenerate from live state.
close_reason: Duplicate of mjolnir-l79.2/.3/.4 (existing epic). Findings folded into those.

title: Gateway: drop-in config dir loader (/etc/mjolnir/gateway.d/*.toml)
description:
Phase 1 of gateway local-routing (docs/plans/gateway-local-routing.md). Let machine-generated routes live separately from the hand-maintained base so an Elixir generator (mjolnir-<phase2>) can own them without co-editing gateway.toml.

Design (native/mjolnir_gateway/src/config.rs): in load(path), after parsing the base file into FileConfig, glob <dir>/gateway.d/*.toml (sorted), parse each into a FileConfig (fields use serde renames: [[domain]]/[[route]]/[[alias]]/[[cert]]), and EXTEND base.routes/.aliases/.certs with each drop-in's before calling validate_and_normalize(merged, Toml). Drop-ins contribute routes/aliases/certs only; apexes/global config stay in the base. SIGHUP already re-runs load() (main.rs:1338-1459), so reload picks up drop-in changes for free.

Notes from live validation:
- Single-file load() today (config.rs:409); no include/merge — this adds it.
- Apex key is [[domain]] with fallthrough, not [[apex]].
- Existing config.alias_shadowed_by_route warning fires when a route shadows an alias; keep that behavior.
- Add unit tests for merge (base + N drop-ins → combined route/alias counts; dedup-by-(apex,subdomain) semantics; malformed drop-in is warn-and-skipped, never crashes load).
Acceptance: drop a file in gateway.d, SIGHUP, route appears; bad file logged + skipped; base-only still works.
close_reason: Duplicate of mjolnir-l79.2/.3/.4 (existing epic). Findings folded into those.

title: Phase 3: gateway local-dial -> Iroh alias failover (Rust)
description: On Disposition::Local dial failure, fall back to handle_iroh_connection if an alias exists for the same (apex,subdomain). Makes stale routes self-healing; multi-host migration seam.

title: exec/execute_command use :infinity vsock timeout — wedged guest blocks VM GenServer mailbox
description: VM.exec/3 and execute_command/2 call Vsock.Connection.exec with :infinity. If a guest wedges mid-exec, the call never returns and blocks the VM GenServer mailbox, so subsequent GenServer.call ops (get_state, etc.) time out and the VM shows as :unreachable. VM.reboot/1 already bypasses this via OS-level CH kill (works regardless of mailbox), so recovery is possible — but a bounded exec timeout (or async exec) would prevent the mailbox-block in the first place. Discovered while fixing mjolnir-l4i. Care: long-running CI jobs legitimately need long timeouts, so a fixed short timeout is wrong — consider a generous bound or making exec not block the GenServer.

title: Gateway: exclude BYO-cert/foreign-apex hosts from ACME SAN derivation
description: derive_san_list currently adds alias FQDNs and none-apex domains to the auto-derived ACME SAN list. For an apex whose DNS zone the Cloudflare token can't manage (e.g. identikey.io), this would make the combined cert order fail and break wildcard renewal. Workaround in prod: explicit [acme].domains pin. Proper fix: hosts served by a [[cert]] (BYO) must be excluded from ACME SAN derivation; reconsider auto-adding alias FQDNs. Parent mjolnir-er5.

title: Gateway: pre-warm Iroh connections for aliased nodes
description: Eliminate cold-start latency on domain->VM requests. When a [[alias]] is configured, eagerly open + keep-alive the Iroh connection to that node so the first request hits a warm pooled connection (no per-request lookup/dial). Keeps ports inside the VM (identity-based) while matching local-dial speed. Chosen direction after zine.identikey.io went live via Iroh alias. Parent mjolnir-er5.

Resolves in classify() before fallthrough, reusing the existing Iroh proxy path. Survives VM respawns (node ID travels with VM identity, unlike a TAP-IP pin). Motivating case: zine.identikey.io → node xebksroii…76njo. Includes config parse/validate, RouteTable.lookup_alias, SAN derivation, tests, example config.

title: Ghost-record cleanup: stranded :running records churn every reconcile tick (17 stranded, 14 DEAD on restart)
description: On a server restart (root@45.76.77.97, 2026-06-24) StartupReconcile rehydrated 17 stranded :running records (s8h parallel resume working, max_concurrency=4); Health.Monitor then declared 14 distinct VMs 'DEAD, not auto-healing'. These are genuinely-dead ghosts (their GenServers exited after failed resume → not in 'mj list' → back to stranded), so each reconcile tick (every 30s) re-attempts resume → fails → DEAD, indefinitely. The durability invariant correctly PRESERVES rootfs/records (no vanishing), but there is no lifecycle end-state for a record that can never resume. mj retire/revive/forget verbs exist (5fu) to clear these by hand; consider an auto-retire policy after N consecutive failed resume attempts so the backlog self-drains. NOTE: VM 076adf62 is ALIVE (exec works) despite a false-positive :egress_blocked (see the ping bug) — do not forget it.
notes: RESOLVED the symptom 2026-06-24: the 16 'ghosts' were NOT dead records — they were live, responsive CI-runner VMs (hostname ci-runner, owner=localhost, 17 live cloud-hypervisor procs) leaked by the Forgejo runner. mj retire 404'd (token owner != localhost) then returned vm_running (they were registered+running, not stranded). Killed all 16 via the localhost API bypass (DELETE /api/vms/:id as owner=localhost); rootfs soft-deleted to @trash (recoverable ~7d). Verified: VM count 17→1, CH procs 17→1, my VM 076adf62 preserved. ROOT CAUSE remains (reframe this issue around it): the Forgejo runner does not tear down per-job VMs, and durability epic r84 then resurrects every leaked :running record on each restart — so leaked CI sandboxes accumulate durably. Fix belongs at the runner teardown path (ensure VM destroy on job completion), not in reconcile. Related: health false-positive 3h3 made them all log as DEAD.

title: Health L2 guest_network probe false-positives :egress_blocked when guest lacks ping (iputils)
description: Mjolnir.Health.GuestNetwork.probe/1 runs 'ping -c1 -W2 1.1.1.1' inside the guest via vsock exec; on failure it returns {:dead, :egress_blocked}. The ubuntu-24.04 base rootfs has NO ping binary ('sh: ping: not found'), so the command fails with command-not-found → echoes NOPING → the VM is classified :dead even though egress works fine (verified live: default route present, DNS resolves, 'curl https://registry.npmjs.org/' → HTTP 200 in 0.6s on VM 076adf62). Net effect: every VM on this base shows overall :dead in 'mj doctor', Health.Monitor logs spurious 'DEAD, not auto-healing', and the heal path needlessly calls reconfigure_network. Found 2026-06-24 verifying a deploy on root@45.76.77.97.
design: Test the property (TCP egress), not a specific tool. Replace the ICMP ping with a no-extra-binary TCP dial, e.g. bash: 'timeout 2 bash -c "exec 3<>/dev/tcp/1.1.1.1/443"' → connect success = egress OK. This matches what apps actually do (TCP) and survives a base image without iputils or with ICMP filtered. Alternative/secondary: add iputils-ping to the base rootfs, but the probe should not depend on it. Keep the NOROUTE fast-path.
acceptance_criteria: A VM with working TCP egress but no ping binary reports L2 guest_network :ok; a VM with a wiped default route still reports :no_default_route; a VM with genuinely blocked egress reports dead.

description: Two cheap changes that unblock compute billing. (1) Move the rendered env render target from /etc/mjolnir/secrets.env (PLAINTEXT on rootfs → baked into every snapshot layer) to /run/mjolnir/secrets.env (tmpfs, RAM-backed, never persisted/snapshotted); service unit uses EnvironmentFile=/run/mjolnir/secrets.env. One-path change in native/mjolnir_guest_agent/src/secrets.rs. (2) Wire secret re-inject on VM wake: control plane re-authorizes the peer and re-pushes secrets over the existing SECRET_INJECT_ALPN path when a dormant VM wakes — so secrets_mode: :persistent VMs (which currently REFUSE dormancy at vm.ex:657 because nobody can supply the LUKS passphrase on auto-wake) can finally scale to zero.
design: Hard rule: cut build-cache layers BEFORE any secret load; build-time secrets live outside the layer cache key AND outside the snapshotted rootfs (inject to tmpfs for the build step, discard before snapshot). Avoid render-into-LUKS (the LUKS file lives on rootfs → snapshot still carries the encrypted secret). Preserves the injector's zero-host-trust posture: passphrase/source stays external.

title: Decouple API availability from VM reconcile on restart
description:
On 'systemctl restart mjolnir', the startup VM reconcile resumes persisted VMs serially (~5s each: TAP create -> guest network -> PTY ready -> resumed). Bandit (the HTTP API on :4000) is the LAST child in Mjolnir.Supervisor, so the API is unavailable until the reconcile finishes. Observed during the 2026-06-23 deploy: 17 VMs => ~17s of API downtime ('connection refused' on :4000) even though 'systemctl is-active' reported active. This scales linearly with VM count: 100+ VMs would mean minutes of API downtime per restart/deploy.

Why it matters: deploys and crashes currently incur downtime proportional to fleet size. As VM count grows (and especially once 'mj deploy' makes long-lived service VMs common), restart-downtime becomes a real availability problem.
design:
Two candidate approaches (not mutually exclusive):
1. Start Bandit BEFORE the reconcile (or move reconcile out of the critical startup path into a background Task/GenServer), so the API serves immediately while VMs resume asynchronously. Tradeoff: API may briefly report VMs as not-yet-resumed; need to handle requests for in-flight VMs gracefully.
2. Parallelize the reconcile (Task.async_stream with bounded concurrency) so N VMs resume in roughly constant time instead of N*5s. Tradeoff: concurrent TAP/hypervisor setup load; cap concurrency.

Recommended: (1) for availability + (2) for total reconcile time. Verify by restarting with many VMs and timing first 200 from /api/health.
acceptance_criteria: API /api/health returns 200 within a few seconds of 'systemctl restart mjolnir' regardless of resumable VM count; VM resume continues in background without blocking the HTTP listener.

title: CLI surface: 'mjolnir publish ./dist' — plain verb, public by default, returns URL
description:
The user-facing publish command. Zero special vocabulary for the common case.

## Why (product principle from design session)
Newcomers must be able to make a static thing public, verifiably from their IdentiKey, WITHOUT memorizing terminology. The verb is 'publish'; verifiability is automatic; recipients/keyspace are progressive-disclosure flags. No Norse codenames in the surface.

## Surface
  mjolnir publish ./dist                  # public by default → prints https://<iroh_id>.vm... + 'signed by <fp>'
  mjolnir publish ./dist --to alice,bob   # gated/recipients
  mjolnir publish ./dist --keyspace team  # group
Only words a newcomer meets: publish, public, recipients, your IdentiKey, a URL.

## Tasks
- Drive Publisher.build_snapshot + publish protocol from the CLI (mjolnir escript / forge-style subcommand).
- Public default; emit the resulting URL + signing fingerprint.
- Wire --to / --keyspace to the keyspace seam.

## Acceptance
- 'mjolnir publish ./dist' on a fresh dir yields a working public URL signed by the user's IdentiKey, with no other flags or jargon required.

Depends on storage + crypto + transport seams.
design: DE-SCOPED by scout: a publish CLI already exists — lib/mix/tasks/mjolnir.sites.publish.ex (Mix.Task, OptionParser, calls Publisher.publish/5) + mjolnir.sites.alias.ex + HTTP router lib/mjolnir/api/sites_router.ex (POST /:fp/:name/snapshot, /head). .6 is now: add lib/mix/tasks/mjolnir.publish.ex mirroring sites.publish.ex but PUBLIC-BY-DEFAULT with friendly output (print URL + signing fingerprint); flags positional dir, --public default | --to | --keyspace. Reuse Publisher.build_snapshot/4 + publish/5. WAIT for .3 to settle publisher.ex signing signature before wiring.

Public-by-default, auto-creates IdentiKey at ~/.config/mjolnir/identikey.json on first run, signs via .3, prints URL+fingerprint. --to/--keyspace rejected with pointer to .5. Will close when .1/.4 close.

title: Keyspace/recipients seam: gated + group modes via identikey-storage-auth + recrypt PRE
description:
Wire the non-public disclosure modes so 'publish --to <recipients>' and 'publish --keyspace <id>' are real, using recrypt's existing primitives.

## Why
This is the architectural payoff: public/gated/group differ ONLY by key disclosure. recrypt already implements keyspaces (identikey-storage-auth: keyspace.rs, capability.rs, grant.rs) and post-quantum proxy recryption (recrypt-core).

## Tasks
- Gated (recipients): encrypt to recipient IdentiKey PRE pubkey(s); per-file wrapped_key in manifest; serve ciphertext+outboard to authenticated caller (Iroh node-id → IdentiKey binding, or capability).
- Group (keyspace): associate site with a recrypt keyspace; server holds per-member recryption keys; recrypt wrapped_key on each authenticated read; atomic revocation by deleting the rk.
- Map CLI flags --to / --keyspace onto these.

## Acceptance
- A recipient can decrypt; a non-recipient cannot.
- Revoking a keyspace member blocks their next read.
- Server never sees plaintext or owner secret in gated/group.

Depends on storage + crypto seams.

title: Transport seam: real Iroh endpoint binding in Sites.Endpoints (reuse VM Iroh path)

## Why
'Get an Iroh address' is step one of the user story. Without a real bind there is no address to publish to. Gateway already resolves <iroh_id>.vm.worldtree.network — this is the missing host-side listener.

## Tasks
- Bind stable Iroh endpoint per site (explicit registration per design §11 decision 1).
- On dial: resolve endpoint → identikey_fp/site → HEAD → serve via Sites.Server.serve/3.
- Confirm gateway round-trips HTTP-over-Iroh to the bound endpoint.

## Acceptance
- A published site is reachable at https://<iroh_id>.vm.worldtree.network.
- Endpoint survives restart (binding persisted as signed record).
design: Scout map (full: scratchpad/scout-map-transport-cli.md). Host-side Iroh bind does NOT exist yet — only guest agent (native/mjolnir_guest_agent/src/iroh.rs run_iroh_server) and gateway (native/mjolnir_gateway) speak Iroh. Sites endpoints.ex:32-35 bind/2 is a stub. Real bind needs a HOST Rust Iroh binding (NIF/sidecar) — same integration decision as .1, so genuinely blocked on .1. Use identikey_fp+site_name as ALPN/routing key.

title: Crypto seam: real MultiSig signing of manifest + HEAD via IdentiKey (replace <<>> stubs)
description:
Replace placeholder signatures (Manifest signatures: <<>>, HeadRecord signature: <<>> — see publisher.ex 'Signatures (Phase 1 stub)') with real signing, and verify on accept.

## Why
The signature IS the 'verifiably from your IdentiKey' value prop. Without it the whole pitch is hollow. Identikey module (lib/mjolnir/sites/identikey.ex) already does ED25519; ML-DSA-87 leg comes from recrypt.

## Tasks
- Sign canonical manifest body + canonical HEAD record body with IdentiKey ED25519 now.
- Verify signature on manifest accept + HEAD update (reject bad sigs; today server would serve unsigned).
- Wire decrypt_public/3 seam (server.ex STUBBED decryption) to real HKDF-derive + XChaCha20.
- Layer ML-DSA-87 (dual-stack MultiSig) once recrypt signing path is reachable — can be a follow-up.

## Acceptance
- Publish produces a signed manifest + signed HEAD.
- Tampered manifest/HEAD is rejected.
- Public-mode serve decrypts real bytes end-to-end (no stub).

title: B2 durability: local hot tier + write-through to Backblaze B2 via recrypt-storage S3
description:
Guarantee the invariant: every published chunk + manifest eventually lands in Backblaze B2 (durable offsite).

## Why
User requirement: 'everything eventually backed up into Backblaze.' B2 is S3-compatible; recrypt-storage's S3 backend already points at custom endpoints (endpoint_url + force_path_style, see its minio() ctor) — B2 is a config change, not new code.

## Decide
Tiered store shape: (a) local FS/BTRFS hot read tier + write-through to B2 directly, or (b) Minio local cache replicating to B2 (matches Duke's prior setup, location currently unknown). Lean (a) — fewer moving parts; Minio only if a local S3 API is independently needed.

## Tasks
- Add B2 credentials/endpoint config (runtime.exs env: B2 key id/app key/endpoint/bucket).

title: Investigate PTY-based exec for CI steps (replace vsock request-response)
description:
Current CI exec uses vsock request-response: send command, block until complete, receive full stdout as one blob. This causes problems for long-running builds:

1. **Output buffering**: stdout is returned as a single string after command finishes. With tail -c 50KB truncation to avoid 64KB vsock frame limit, we lose most build output. No real-time streaming to Forgejo logs.

2. **Connection fragility**: during a 45s+ cargo build, the vsock connection appears idle (no data flowing). OOM kills or any guest agent issue drops the connection, losing the entire exec result with no partial output.

3. **Timeout complexity**: GenServer.call with :infinity timeout works but masks connection drops. A PTY channel would detect disconnects immediately.

4. **No interactivity**: can't ctrl-c a hung build, can't stream progress bars, can't tail logs in real-time.

Mjolnir already supports PTY channels (vsock channels 1-255 for binary streams). The guest agent has PtyOpen/PtyResize/PtyClose handling with full terminal multiplexing. The runner could:

- Open a PTY channel per step via POST /api/vms/:id/pty
- Send the command as input to the PTY
- Stream output in real-time over the binary channel
- Detect exit via shell prompt or exit code sentinel
- Forward each line to Forgejo's UpdateLog RPC as it arrives

This would also enable the syslog-based log streaming we designed (Mjolnir.Syslog.Listener routing to EventBus) to complement PTY output for background processes.

Alternatively, add a streaming exec endpoint to the Mjolnir API (SSE or chunked HTTP) that wraps the vsock exec with progressive output forwarding, avoiding the frame size limit entirely.

Ref: vsock connection drop during cargo build (session 2026-06-08), Vsock.Connection.exec timeout, PTY support in guest agent (src/pty.rs).

Failure mode: the action directory gets copied but node execution fails (likely path/permission issue in Copy or missing node_modules). title: Research/impl: self-hosted Iroh relay for multi-host cloud
description:
Today both the guest agent (native/mjolnir_guest_agent/src/iroh.rs) and the gateway use iroh::endpoint::presets::N0 — number0's PUBLIC relay network — for connection rendezvous + NAT-traversal fallback. The gateway↔co-located-VM cold-start (~7s) is being fixed by local TCP routing (epic mjolnir-l79), which removes Iroh from the co-located path entirely, so a self-hosted relay buys NOTHING for the single-host case (direct beats even a LAN-local relay).

Self-hosted relay becomes valuable ONLY once we run a multi-host cloud:
- Faster cross-host connection establishment (relay RTT drops from public-internet to our own regional/backbone).
- No hard dependency on number0's relay infra (reliability, privacy, control).
- Enables the 'any local Mjolnir VM routes globally without Tailscale' vision on our own rendezvous.
- Pair it with Iroh direct-address hints (connection_info/1 already returns IP hints, not just relay URLs) so cross-host dials skip the relay when a direct path exists.

Scope when picked up:
- Stand up iroh-relay (DERP-like) on our host(s); configure guest + gateway endpoints to use it (relay map / custom preset) instead of / in addition to N0.
- Decide relay placement/topology for the fleet; health + failover to N0.
- Measure cross-host cold-connect latency vs N0 baseline.

GATED ON multi-host. Not actionable while single-host. See docs/plans/gateway-local-routing.md (self-hosted-relay analysis) and docs/forge-architecture.md (multi-host direction).

description:
Once Mjolnir spans multiple hosts, stand up our own Iroh relay instead of relying on number0's public relays (iroh::endpoint::presets::N0). 

WHY (from gateway local-routing investigation, docs/plans/gateway-local-routing.md): the ~7s zine cold-start was Iroh global-overlay connection setup (relay rendezvous + hole-punch) to a CO-LOCATED VM. That specific case is now fixed by direct local TCP routing (epic mjolnir-l79) — Iroh is removed from the co-located hot path. So a self-hosted relay does NOT help the single-host case and is explicitly NOT needed now.

It becomes valuable in the MULTI-HOST future:
- Faster cross-host connection establishment (relay RTT drops from internet-scale to our own regional/LAN relay).
- No dependency on number0's public relay infra (reliability, privacy, control, no rate limits).
- Enables 'any local Mjolnir VM routes globally without Tailscale' (the hole-punch/discovery rendezvous is ours).

Pair with: injecting direct socket-address hints into the Iroh EndpointAddr (connection_info/1 already returns IP hints, not just relay URLs) so cross-host dials that CAN go direct skip the relay entirely. The relay is the fallback for NAT-blocked paths.

Scope when picked up: deploy iroh-relay binary (host config via Forge systemd_unit), point guest+gateway endpoints at our relay (replace/augment presets::N0), TLS/domain for the relay, health monitoring. Blocked on multi-host cluster layer (roadmap: 'Multi-node cluster').

Not a priority until multi-host lands.

title: Gateway: local-route dial failure falls back to Iroh alias (self-healing)
description:
Phase 3 of gateway local-routing (docs/plans/gateway-local-routing.md). Make a stale local [[route]] non-fatal and establish the multi-host seam (local-first, Iroh-for-remote).

Today (main.rs:868-881) a Disposition::Local dial failure returns 502 — it does NOT try Iroh. Goal: if the local backend is unreachable AND an Iroh alias exists for the same (apex, subdomain), fall back to handle_iroh_connection.

DESIGN WRINKLE found in live validation: the config loader DROPS an alias that is shadowed by a route (logs config.alias_shadowed_by_route; alias_count→0). So there is no alias left in the RouteTable to fall back to. This is therefore primarily a LOADER change, not just a handler change:
- Retain shadowed aliases in a side map (apex,subdomain)→Alias instead of dropping them, OR
- Let a [[route]] carry an optional fallback node z32.
Then in handle_connection, on Local dial failure, look up the retained alias and call handle_iroh_connection; only 502 if no fallback exists.
Multi-host relevance: the generator writes local routes only for VMs on this host; VMs elsewhere stay aliases; this failover covers VM migration and the moment a route goes stale before regeneration. Pairs with Phase 2.
Acceptance: kill the app VM's :3000, request still succeeds via Iroh (logs route=local then fallback=iroh); with no alias, returns 502 as today.
close_reason: Duplicate of mjolnir-l79.2/.3/.4 (existing epic). Findings folded into those.

title: Research: VM TAP IP hash collisions at scale (Network.allocate_ip)
description:
Network.allocate_ip/1 (lib/mjolnir/network.ex:149-179) derives a VM's TAP IP from SHA256(vm_id) into the 10.200.0.0/10 range (~4M usable addrs), avoiding .0/.255 last octet. It is deterministic (good: stable across restart/restore) but does NOT check for collisions — two distinct vm_ids can hash to the same IP. At current scale (handful of VMs) the birthday-bound collision probability is negligible, so this is NOT urgent. File for when we scale.

Scope of research:
- Quantify collision probability vs concurrent-VM count (birthday problem over the usable address space).
- Decide mitigation: (a) collision detection + linear probe / rehash on allocate, (b) registry-backed IP leasing instead of pure hashing, (c) widen range / restructure subnetting, (d) per-host IP namespaces once multi-host lands.
- Consider interaction with gateway local-routing (docs/plans/gateway-local-routing.md): if a generated [[route]] points at a colliding/stale IP, the Iroh-alias fallback (Phase 3) should cover it, but routing correctness still needs a unique IP.
- Note multi-host: deterministic-from-vm_id is attractive for stateless routing, but collisions become more likely and cross-host IP reuse needs thought.

Not a priority right now — /10 is generous. Revisit at ~thousands of concurrent VMs/host or when multi-host routing is designed.

title: Bind host forgejo to 127.0.0.1:3000 instead of 0.0.0.0:3000
description: The host's forgejo service binds 0.0.0.0:3000 (all interfaces), but the web gateway only ever proxies to it via mimir.worldtree.network → 127.0.0.1:3000. Because it listens on all interfaces, forgejo:3000 is currently reachable from the VM TAP networks (10.0.0.0/8) as well, which is unnecessary attack surface. Rebinding to 127.0.0.1:3000 shrinks its reachable surface to just the gateway's loopback proxy path. This is a host-service config tweak (forgejo app.ini HTTP_ADDR / listen address), not a Mjolnir VM change. Surfaced during a listener/port scan of the host.
notes:
Investigated on host (45.76.77.97). NOT actioned — premise was incorrect. Findings:
1. UFW is active with INPUT policy DROP. The only allow rule for :3000 is '10.0.0.0/8 -> 10.255.255.1:3000' (# VMs to Forgejo). There is NO rule permitting the public interface 45.76.77.97:3000, so despite the 0.0.0.0 bind the public exposure is already firewalled off at the packet layer.
2. TAP reachability is REQUIRED, not surplus: the forgejo-runner registered its instance address as http://10.255.255.1:3000, and CI jobs inside VMs reach forgejo over the TAP gateway IP for git checkout. Binding 127.0.0.1 would break Actions.
3. HTTP_ADDR takes a single address, so it cannot serve both loopback (gateway proxy, gateway.toml backend=127.0.0.1:3000) and 10.255.255.1 (VM jobs) at once. The only defense-in-depth variant (bind 10.255.255.1 + repoint gateway) was considered and declined as not worth the restart/coupling given UFW already covers the public surface.
Conclusion: current posture (0.0.0.0 bind + UFW default-deny + single VM-subnet allow) is acceptable. Closing as already-mitigated.

title: Parallel track — Recrypt integration: host a recryption proxy, map keyspace to VM keypair, build guest recrypt-client
description: End-state secrets transport, replacing P1.5's re-inject. Host a recryption proxy on Mjolnir (recrypt engine at ~/work/IdentiKey/recrypt: lattice PRE via OpenFHE + classical EC, KEM-DEM, Gordian Envelope, multi-sig auth — transforms ciphertext-for-owner into ciphertext-for-VM without decrypting). Map a keyspace to the VM's OWN keypair; recrypt the secret bundle to the VM key on wake; the guest decrypts in RAM with a key only it holds. Host/proxy never see plaintext; revocation = drop the re-encryption key; and the persistent LUKS volume can go away ENTIRELY — removing the dormancy refusal at its root. Build the guest-side recrypt-client (currently a stub).

title: P3 — Operability: layer GC/prune (qgroup metering), health-gated releases, multi-process apps

Two GC classes: cache layers (LRU-evict freely under pressure, light/no billing) vs release layers (never auto-deleted, user prunes via mj deploy prune --keep N, billed). Bake owner_id + qgroup attribution into the layer schema from day one — retrofitting onto already-shared snapshots is painful. (2) Health-gated releases: probe GET / (or configured healthcheck) in the new VM before flipping the URL; enables rollback-on-failure. (3) Multi-process apps (Procfile web+worker): start with one VM, multiple systemd units.
